transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-07-29
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Tom (Redwood SE), Elena (Redwood SE), Jenna (Arclight CTO), Ravi (Infra), Lila (Product), Sam (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Arclight is evaluating Redwood for a hybrid reseller/integrator flow where they will embed Redwood inference into their EdgeWeave product. Primary concerns: VPC peering, KMS/encryption, air-gapped deployment options, performance across variable batch sizes, and cost modeling for dedicated GPU pools. They want a pilot to validate latency SLOs and integration with their private networking. Next steps: Redwood to send security docs, benchmark plan, and pricing; schedule pilot.

Transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone thanks for joining, good to meet you all. quick intro, i'm Maya, AE on the Redwood partner org, and Tom and Elena from our solutions team with me.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Hi Maya, this is Jenna. We run the engineering org at Arclight, thanks for the time.
00:16 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Ravi here, infra, hi.
00:19 Speaker 4 (Lila): Lila, product.
00:21 Speaker 1 (Maya): Awesome. Quick framing -- we hear you want to embed inference into your EdgeWeave appliance and want to understand fit for VPC-turned-on premises and what the pilot looks like. is that right?
00:33 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Yes, exactly. We're a systems integrator, and a bunch of our customers want a turnkey LLM inference capability in the appliance. main asks are: private network only, KMS integration, and predictable latency.
00:46 Speaker 5 (Tom): Got it. When you say private network only, do you mean fully air-gapped or VPC peering with our control plane?
00:55 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Mostly VPC peering for the first pass, but some high-security customers will ask for an air-gapped bundle. we want both paths to be possible eventually.
01:05 Speaker 6 (Sam): and security wise we need to see KMS/HSM support, audit logs, RBAC mapping to our IAM, and of course SOC2 evidence.
01:15 Speaker 5 (Tom): Absolutely — Redwood supports customer-managed KMS, we can run the private control plane in your VPC or in a dedicated subnet. audit logs and RBAC map to SAM L? SAML? (laugh) sorry -- SAML/SSO, yes.
01:29 Speaker 6 (Sam): SAML yes. Good.
01:33 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick qualification Qs: what models are you expecting to serve (open models, fine-tuned, embedding workloads?), and approximate QPS / concurrent sessions?
01:42 Speaker 4 (Lila): Primary is text generation assistant (customer ops assistant) and then some embeddings for semantic search. we'll probably start with a 7B-13B open model variant but want to preserve ability to move to quantized 30B later. concurrency target is 200 concurrent small sessions, peak QPS around 60 requests/sec, average token length ~150.
01:04 Speaker 5 (Tom): (note: timestamp got slightly off) okay that helps. for 13B quantized we can talk about dedicated pools vs hosted. latency SLO you're aiming for?
02:10 Speaker 4 (Lila): sub-300ms per token ideally but we're flexible; more important is tail latency and predictability.
02:21 Speaker 5 (Tom): Great. I'd suggest a dedicated reserved pool for mixed workloads to keep tails tight; we also have prefix caching/KV cache options to lower per-token cost for repeated prompts.
02:34 Speaker 2 (Jenna): can you explain the KV cache bit again? last call i heard something about prefix cache but the terms blur.
02:42 Speaker 5 (Tom): Sure — KV cache is per-request state we keep in memory so re-generation or continuation is faster. prefix caching helps if you have a set of common prompt prefixes across customers, it avoids re-computation. both help latency and cost.
02:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): also on routing: Redwood can do smart routing by policy — e.g., route to a cheaper quantized variant when cost tier is hit, or fallback to a smaller model on high load. does that align with your needs?
03:09 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Yes, fallback is important. we won't accept a full outage during spikes. automatic fallback would help.
03:15 Speaker 6 (Sam): about compliance, are there customers that will require whole logs not to leave the premises?
03:22 Speaker 5 (Tom): For fully air-gapped we can plan an on-prem package where logs stay in your environment; for VPC peering we can limit retention and stream logs to your SIEM.
03:34 Speaker 6 (Sam): good. also we need KMS support; we use HashiVault and AWS KMS depending on customer.
03:41 Speaker 5 (Tom): Redwood supports customer-managed KMS; HashiVault has some additional integration steps but it's workable. we'll put details in the security pack.
03:48 Speaker 4 (Lila): cost model — how do you price dedicated pools vs hosted? we need to model for reseller margins.
03:55 Speaker 1 (Maya): hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings), dedicated is monthly reserved capacity; for partners we have reseller uplift options and committed capacity discounts. we'll share a partner pricing sheet.
04:08 Speaker 2 (Jenna): do you have examples of integrators doing this? use cases?
04:14 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes — a couple of channel partners embed Redwood into appliances; we can anonymize case studies. I'll include a short partner one-pager.
04:22 Speaker 4 (Lila): integration effort — how invasive is the control plane peering?
04:28 Speaker 5 (Tom): For VPC peering you typically open a set of egress rules and SSO connectors; if you want the private control plane running in your VPC we package a helm chart/runbook. it's not trivial but it's standard infra work.
04:40 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Helm chart yes please. our infra team prefers declarative deploys. what's the minimum HW for on-prem inference?
04:49 Speaker 5 (Tom): depends on model. for a 13B quantized single-instance you need at least a 80GB GPU class card or multiple 48GB with NVLink for larger models; for 7B you can run on 48GB cards. We'll attach hardware guidance.
05:02 Speaker 3 (Ravi): Our EdgeWeave appliances currently run dual A40s (48GB each) and a light NVMe pool. sounds like the 7B path is safe initially.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Tom): yep that's consistent. for 13B quantized you'd want a 80GB or sharded 48GB setup.
05:18 Speaker 6 (Sam): question on telemetry: can we push metrics to our Prometheus + Grafana stack?
05:24 Speaker 5 (Tom): Yes, we have exporters and can forward per-route metrics. also Redwood Console has tracing hooks but you can ingest into your observability.
05:34 Speaker 2 (Jenna): benching — what would you want from us to run a pilot?
05:39 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll need a representative workload (prompt distribution, token lengths, concurrency), network topology (VPC peering endpoints), and a list of success criteria: e.g., p95 latency < 500ms for 90% of requests, error rate < 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens < $X.
05:55 Speaker 4 (Lila): Ok we'll put that together. timeline we want: 6-week pilot, then go-to-market for a tranche of customers.
06:03 Speaker 1 (Maya): Sounds reasonable. We'll draft a 6-week plan in the pilot proposal.
06:08 Speaker 3 (Ravi): a nit: we have customers in EU and APAC, can Redwood regionally pin models? we need data residency guarantees.
06:18 Speaker 5 (Tom): yes, Redwood supports model pinning by region and private deployments in regions; we'll document region options and latency tradeoffs.
06:27 Speaker 6 (Sam): also encryption at rest across NVMe — we need to see that and HSM-based key protections.
06:33 Speaker 5 (Tom): We'll include HSM/KMS options in the pack.
06:36 Speaker 2 (Jenna): any limitations around model quantization? sometimes quantization regresses on hallucination rates.
06:44 Speaker 5 (Tom): Correct — there's a tradeoff. Redwood Optimize gives quantization recommendations per workload and we run evals against your prompt set to measure quality delta before recommending.
06:56 Speaker 4 (Lila): That eval piece is useful. would you run with our prompt set?
06:59 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, for pilot we'll run a small eval with your holdout prompts, measure output quality and latency, and include thresholds in success criteria.
07:08 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Great. Do you support function/tool calling or streaming for real-time agents?
07:14 Speaker 5 (Tom): We support streaming responses and tool/function calling primitives; the runtime keeps KV cache and streaming lowers perceived latency for agents.
07:23 Speaker 4 (Lila): What about rollouts — can we do canary deploys between model variants so we can test regressions?
07:29 Speaker 5 (Tom): Yes, Redwood has rollout policies for canary and weighted A/B with automatic fallback. we'll include a runbook.
07:36 Speaker 6 (Sam): On liability and data, our legal will want to see DPA and specifics about data retention and deletion.
07:42 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll attach our DPA and standard reseller agreement; please flag any specific redlines early.
07:48 Speaker 3 (Ravi): One operational thing — if we do VPC peering, do you need a public endpoint for telemetry or is it fully private?
07:56 Speaker 5 (Tom): It can be fully private; we can stream telemetry over the peered connection to your collectors.
08:04 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Pricing again: if we resell, what's typical margin? we need to model for channel pricing.
08:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): We'll send a partner sheet with suggested margins. There's room on committed capacity discounts.
08:20 Speaker 4 (Lila): Any known integration pitfalls to watch out for?
08:25 Speaker 5 (Tom): In my experience: network MTU and throughput limits on appliances (affects streaming), KMS latency for key unwrap on large volumes, and model quantization quality regressions. Also version pinning — make sure you pin model versions in production.
08:40 Speaker 3 (Ravi): good notes.
08:43 Speaker 2 (Jenna): curious: competitors? who do we expect to compare you to?
08:47 Speaker 1 (Maya): Often NimbusCloud for managed endpoints and AuroraCompute for dedicated GPU contracts; also some customers evaluate building on open-source runtimes, but then they carry ops.
08:59 Speaker 2 (Jenna): got it.
09:02 Speaker 4 (Lila): okay what's the next step, recap?
09:06 Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap: Redwood will send security pack (SOC2, KMS, HSM notes), partner pricing sheet, pilot proposal with success criteria and a 6-week timeline, and a benchmark plan. Arclight will send representative workload, current topology (VPC & appliance specs), and compliance questions. We'll schedule a 2-hour bench session next week with Ravi and Tom.
09:29 Speaker 2 (Jenna): Perfect.
09:31 Speaker 6 (Sam): small follow-up: if we need an on-prem air-gapped bundle will that be a different commercial track?
09:37 Speaker 1 (Maya): Yes, on-prem air-gapped tends to be an enterprise/private deployment with a platform license and professional services. We'll put that in the proposal as an optional path.
09:49 Speaker 2 (Jenna): makes sense.
09:51 Speaker 1 (Maya): Anything else from the Arclight side?
09:54 Speaker 4 (Lila): Not from product, we'll gather prompts.
09:56 Speaker 3 (Ravi): i'll send hardware inventory.
09:58 Speaker 6 (Sam): i'll compile the compliance Qs.
10:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. we'll follow up via email with the materials and a calendar invite for the bench. thanks everyone.

Notes on transcription: there are occasional mis-recognitions (e.g., 'Redbud' instead of Redwood, 'SAM L' for SAML). speakers sometimes overlap and timestamps drift slightly.
